prompt:
Implement `resolve_order(dependencies)` in `deps.py`. `dependencies` is a dict mapping each node name (a string) to a list of node names it depends on (nodes that must come before it). A node that only ever appears inside another node's dependency list, and never as a key of its own, is still part of the graph and simply has no dependencies.

- Returns a list containing every node exactly once, ordered so every node comes after all of its dependencies.
- When more than one valid order is possible at a given step, always pick the lexicographically smallest node name among those whose dependencies are all already placed.
- Raises `ValueError` if the graph has a cycle (a node that (directly or indirectly) depends on itself counts as a cycle).
- Raises `TypeError` if `dependencies` is not a `dict`.
- This runs on large dependency graphs, so it must stay fast: it needs to handle graphs with up to 50,000 nodes quickly. Repeatedly scanning the whole node set to find the next ready node (an O(n²) approach) will be too slow.
